subject: FinTrack Private VPC path selection and allowlist — post-demo next steps
messages:
From: Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@fintrack.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: FinTrack - Redwood evaluation — quick follow-up

Thanks again for the demo this morning. A couple of follow-ups from my side as we evaluate hosting options (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

High level: our security and network team prefer Private VPC (we run several regulated workloads in our primary VPC). Before we proceed I need to clarify a few infra items so we can get internal sign-off: 

- PrivateLink vs VPC Peering: which approach will give us the most predictable egress behavior? We need static egress IPs for third-party integrations.
- Who terminates TLS and where do we perform mutual auth?
- KMS: We will likely want customer-managed keys — is HSM/KMS integration supported in your Private offering?
- Allowlist: can you provide a sample allowlist/cidr format for our firewall team?
- SOC2 / evidentiary artifacts: our compliance folks will ask for audit-log retention and SOC2 report pointers.
- Timeline: target internal deliverable is to choose a hosting path by 2026-10-01, with a staging window in mid-Oct.

Can someone on your side own a short tech ops call with our network engineer (cc ops@fintrack.com) this week? I'll share windows after I sync with them.

Samuel
Senior Cloud Architect
FinTrack
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@fintrack.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 17:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinTrack - Redwood evaluation — quick follow-up

Thanks Samuel — great questions and totally reasonable timeline. Quick recap and proposed next steps below. Attaching a short screener that our private deployments team uses to speed qualification (fintrack-privatenet-screener.pdf).

Recap / recommendations:
- PrivateLink vs Peering: both are supported. Recommendation guidance:
  - VPC Peering if you prefer network-native routing and have existing VPC CIDR capacity; peering gives low-network-hop latency and transparent routing but requires explicit CIDR management.
  - PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink / endpoint) if you need fine-grained service-level isolation and simpler egress control from Redwood's side; PrivateLink can be easier for multi-tenant connectors but may require NAT/egress handling on your side depending on flows.
- Static egress IPs: we can provide fixed outbound IPs via our egress NAT pools when using a peering/deployed private connector; if you need provider-side fixed IPs for third-party APIs we can arrange dedicated egress ranges on Dedicated/Private setups.
- TLS / mTLS: by default TLS is terminated at the Redwood Private service edge; we support mutual TLS for customer authentication and can terminate TLS at your side if you route through an internal proxy — we'll note this as an ops decision.
- KMS integration: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations in Private deployments. We will need the KMS ARN and an access model to define who rotates keys.
- SOC2 & audit logs: we have an SOC2 report and can share standard evidentiary artifacts; audit-log retention windows are configurable for Private deployments.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
1) Tech ops working session (30–45m) with your network engineer and our netops engineer (Ben) — topics: peering vs PrivateLink, required CIDR ranges, allowed ports, egress model, TLS/mTLS.
2) We send our network allowlist template (CSV) and a short checklist for KMS onboarding.
3) Post-call we’ll produce a one-page decision memo with recommended hosting mode and estimated effort.

Availability: Ben (netops) is available Wed/Thu 09:00–12:00 PT. Please share a window that works for your engineer or we can propose specific times once you confirm.

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: fintrack-privatenet-screener.pdf (1 page)

> 
> Recap / recommendations:
> - PrivateLink vs Peering: both are supported...

Thanks Stephanie — helpful summary. A couple clarifications from our ops lead (cc'd):

- Preference: we prefer VPC Peering for latency and because our existing firewall rules are easier to manage that way.
- Egress IPs: we need a list of provider-owned outbound IPs that Redwood will NAT to, or confirmation you'll accept our NATed egress from our side (we currently NAT through a managed egress pool).
- TLS: we will terminate TLS on our side; can Redwood support mTLS between our proxy and the Redwood private endpoint?
- KMS: we will supply a KMS ARN; need details on key rotation responsibilities.

We have a network engineer free Wed 09:30–10:15 PT — can you confirm Ben for that slot?

Samuel
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Lee <samuel.lee@fintrack.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FinTrack - Redwood evaluation — quick follow-up

Samuel — thanks and confirmed for Wed 09:30 PT (I’ll join as netops). Quick answers ahead of the call and attached allowlist template (redwood-network-allowlist-template.csv):

- Egress IPs: for a peering setup you can manage NAT on your side; if you'd prefer Redwood-managed static egress we can allocate provider-side egress ranges (this requires a short procurement/ops ticket and is often used for third-party API allowlisting).
- mTLS: yes, we support mTLS between your proxy and our private endpoint. We will exchange cert fingerprints and provide instructions for CN/SAN expectations.
- KMS: customer-managed KMS is supported. Typical model: you provide the KMS ARN and permissions for Redwood service principal to encrypt/decrypt; key rotation remains with your security team, we recommend an annual rotation with monitoring alerts — we can document the exact IAM policy.
- Ports & protocols: default port 443 for API traffic. If you have embedded agents calling back to external services, include those CIDRs in the allowlist.

Action items before call:
1) Samuel / ops to populate the attached CSV with (a) VPC CIDR(s), (b) contact for procurement, (c) desired egress model ("client-managed NAT" or "redwood-managed egress").
2) We'll prepare an internal rollout estimate and a one-page decision memo after the call.

Attachments: redwood-network-allowlist-template.csv

Looking forward to Wed.

Ben Carter
NetOps Lead, Redwood Inference
